text:
Where, you say, now, are those steps

through the unknown, in the

first solitude.


Latitude of the vines, far away.

The final sun opened its

remote flank

over the stones, over the leaves, in a last

dream, the end of summer.

It was dusk,

it was another land, perhaps darker,

the red earth, yes,

as if some ember of the origin

still breathed in it,

beyond, at the end of all impermanence,

as in the distance.


Arcane light,

suspension of suns over the plantains.


It was

all that certainly burned in the invisible.

It was only the light,

as if empty, and as if it could see

its dark burning

in the ferns, in the sky,

over the earth.

Then, to return from there,

over the same steps,

but now, I knew, unrepeatable.

The house

was always a thing of light.

From that day it knew the shadow, or its

sign.

There, upon a stone,

inscribed in the remote, beneath

the wounded light,

a sign for summer, the end, beside the vines,


the end that was an origin,

A., September, the suns, upon an

extreme stone.


From “White Fire,” 1992

translation.title: A Stone, Memory
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish rendering; the fractured spacing and recursive memory image are preserved, with no title or source-text repair beyond evident line joining.
